title.headingHtml: What did Utahns have to say about AI?
title.bodyHtml: Utah Common Ground and its partners talked to over 400 residents from around the region to hear what they thought should be done about AI.

demogs.body: People across the region participated in this conversation, both through our Open Poll and live conversations.

groups.heading: Participants represented a range of perspectives on AI…
groups.body: We found three opinion groups based on our analysis of people's voting patterns. Click each group to learn about what distinguished them from the rest.

consensus.heading: …but we found a lot of common ground.
consensus.body: Despite their differences, almost everyone agreed on the importance of transparency and community involvement in AI-related decision-making.

cta.heading: Now is the time to act for the future of our communities.
cta.bodyHtml: We're organizing a Civic Assembly in September 2026, where 30-40 residents will develop policies to make sure the public has a meaningful role in the government's AI-related decisions. You are invited to participate; selected delegates will receive a $250 stipend.
